name: Isshido Ramen
notes: No website in the work list; address confirmed exact match (8250 Mira Mesa Blvd Ste A, San Diego, CA 92126) against order.online's own page. Tried the restaurant's own Toast storefronts first (order.toasttab.com/online/isshido-ramen-8250-a-mira-mesa-boulevard and the toast.app redirect of toasttab.com/local/order/...): both parse cleanly via window.__OO_STATE__ with a real Chrome UA but hasOnlineOrderingModule is false and only restaurant metadata is present, no menu/items -- Toast is not usable here. Used order.online's escaped Next.js RSC flight payload instead (MenuBookCategory/MenuPageItemList/MenuPageItem objects), which held the complete 10-category, 115-item catalog (Starters, Ramen, Noodle Choice, Yakisoba, Rice Bento, Rice Bowl, Family Package, Beverage, Kids Menu, Condiments & Utensil) plus a 'Most Ordered' carousel whose 10 items all duplicated items already in real categories (dropped). Dropped 6 items with no price: 2 'NOT FOR SALE' noodle-choice modifier options, and 4 free condiments (No Utensils, Disposable Utensils, Soy Sauce, Chili Oil). MARKUP DETECTED: dividing every remaining price by 1.15 landed 107 of 109 items within a cent of a clean nickel-rounded base value (mostly X.95, e.g. Chicken Paitan $17.19 / 1.15 = $14.9478 -> reconstructing $14.95 x 1.15 = $17.1925 rounds to exactly $17.19) -- a uniform 15% online-ordering surcharge, well above the ~17-23% organic-noise band. Recorded the reconstructed base price (the number that, times 1.15 and rounded to the cent, reproduces order.online's displayed price) for those 107 items rather than the inflated number, since this is a single-channel source and the divisor pattern is unambiguous. Kept order.online's own displayed price as-is (did not reconstruct) for 2 items that did not fit the pattern cleanly: Shishito Peppers ($10.95, /1.15=$9.52, not a clean nickel) and Scallop Sashimi ($18.95, /1.15=$16.48, not a clean nickel) -- these may already be un-marked-up or use different rounding; flagged rather than guessed.
